Home Paths About FAQ Schedule
Compassionate clinical care
{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}}

Practical questions, answered plainly

Below are common questions I hear from prospective clients. If you don't see what you need, please reach out—I'll respond within 48 hours.

How do I know if short-term work is enough?
We begin with a focused intake to clarify goals. Short-term work is well-suited to targeted skill-building or coping with a specific stressor; longer care supports deeper patterns and trauma processing.
Do you take insurance?
I do not bill insurance directly in most cases. I provide documents (superbills) you can submit for possible reimbursement. We can discuss options during a consult.
What if I'm in crisis?
If you are in immediate danger or at risk of harming yourself or others, call emergency services or your local crisis line. Therapy sessions are not emergency services.
How do cancellations work?
Please notify me 48 hours before your appointment to avoid a cancellation fee. Late cancellations and no-shows may incur the full session rate.
Are telehealth sessions available?
Yes. I offer secure video sessions for clients in {{STATE}}. Some clients prefer a mix of in-person and telehealth to fit their schedule.
How long before I notice change?
People notice different shifts at different times. Many clients experience practical relief from stressors within a few sessions; deeper pattern change often takes more consistent work. We review progress regularly.
What are your specialties?
I work with anxiety, trauma-informed care, relationship transitions, burnout, and life-stage shifts. I draw from trauma-aware psychotherapies and mindfulness-based approaches. I do not provide medication management.

Mini self-check you can try now

  1. Pause and take three slow breaths.
  2. Notice one feeling in your body and name it (e.g., 'tension' or 'sadness').
  3. Ask: 'What would be one small step I could take this week?'
Still have questions? I'm happy to help.
Reach out

Scope, limits, and confidentiality

Sessions are confidential within legal limits. I will discuss limits to confidentiality, record-keeping, and data privacy during intake. I do not provide emergency services. If you're in crisis, contact emergency services immediately.

Schedule a session or a free check-in

Choose a quick consult to confirm fit or book a full session. I offer both single-session and cohort-style care.

Booking options

Intro Consult — Free (15 min)

A brief call to review needs, logistics, and fit. Not clinical time. Use when you want to ask questions before committing.

Request a consult

Single Session — One-off

$160 • 50 minutes

Book this when you need targeted support or an initial assessment. A focused planning note will be provided.

Book a session

Cohort Course — The Walk-Together Program

$880 • 6 sessions over 12 weeks

A moderated cohort for skill-building: weekly practices, guided reflections, and community learning. Cohorts begin seasonally; inquire to join the next group.

Join waitlist

Ongoing Care — Renewed Path

$135/session with a 12-session commitment

A reduced per-session rate for clients committing to steady work. Includes quarterly reviews and optional resource summaries.

Start ongoing care

What happens after you request?

  1. We schedule a brief consult to confirm fit and availability.
  2. If you choose to proceed, we'll set your initial session and share intake forms.
  3. We review goals in session and set a recommended rhythm for follow-up.

Intake snapshot

To make the most of our first session, please be prepared to share:

  • Current concerns and what you hope will change
  • Relevant mental health history
  • Any safety concerns

You'll receive secure intake forms and a consent packet after scheduling.

Small habits I invite clients to try

  • Daily 60-second breathing pause
  • Weekly reflection: one thing that felt different
  • Micro-boundary: 10 minutes of protected time each day

Notes on care & limits

Therapy provided is confidential within legal and ethical boundaries. I do not provide crisis response. If you're in immediate danger, call emergency services.
